organization: National Academies / Food and Nutrition Board
title: Dietary Reference Intakes / protein RDA
key_support: Adult protein RDA is expressed relative to body weight; 0.8 g/kg/day is the reference value used for healthy adults.
limitations: Not a dish-level threshold; requirements differ with body size and physiological/activity context.

organization: Journal of Cachexia, Sarcopenia and Muscle
title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of protein intake to support muscle mass and function in healthy adults
key_support: Increasing daily protein intake produced small additional gains in lean body mass and some strength outcomes, mainly in resistance-exercise settings.
limitations: Effects depend on exercise, age and total intake; physical-function effects were small or unclear.

title: Calcium — Health Professional Fact Sheet
key_support: Calcium is central to bone structure; adult recommended intakes vary by age and sex, commonly 1000–1200 mg/day.
limitations: Food calcium, supplements and fracture-prevention claims are not interchangeable.

title: Association Between Calcium or Vitamin D Supplementation and Fracture Incidence in Community-Dwelling Older Adults
key_support: Calcium, vitamin D, or combined supplementation was not associated with lower fracture incidence in this population.
limitations: Does not imply calcium adequacy is unimportant; intervention was supplementation in a specific older population.

title: Iron — Health Professional Fact Sheet
key_support: Iron requirements vary strongly by sex and pregnancy; vegetarian requirements are higher because nonheme iron is less bioavailable.
limitations: Dish total iron does not identify heme/nonheme fractions or individual iron status.

title: Screening and Supplementation for Iron Deficiency and Iron Deficiency Anemia During Pregnancy
key_support: Routine prenatal iron supplementation reduced iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anemia at term.
limitations: Evidence for broader maternal and infant clinical outcomes was limited or showed no clear benefit.

title: Folate — Health Professional Fact Sheet
key_support: Natural food folate, folic acid and DFE are distinct; DFE accounts for higher bioavailability of folic acid.
limitations: A source field labeled FolicAcid cannot be assumed to represent food folate, synthetic folic acid, or DFE without source documentation.

title: Effects and safety of periconceptional oral folate supplementation for preventing birth defects
key_support: Periconceptional folic acid supplementation reduced neural tube defects.
limitations: This evidence cannot be mapped directly to a dish FolicAcid field until nutrient-form semantics are resolved.

title: Dietary Cholesterol and Cardiovascular Risk: A Science Advisory
key_support: Observational evidence generally does not show a significant CVD association, while many intervention meta-analyses associate higher cholesterol intake with higher total or LDL cholesterol.
limitations: A specific dietary cholesterol target is difficult to operationalize; guidance emphasizes overall dietary patterns and saturated-fat context.

title: 2019 Guideline on the Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease
key_support: Primary prevention guidance prioritizes healthy dietary patterns rather than isolated nutrient labels.

title: 2020 ACR Guideline for the Management of Gout
key_support: The guideline conditionally recommends limiting purine intake in patients with gout; certainty for lifestyle recommendations is low.
limitations: Applies to gout, not the general population; diet usually produces only modest changes in serum urate and does not replace urate-lowering therapy when indicated.

organization: Journal of Health, Population and Nutrition
title: Impact of lifestyle factors and dietary patterns on serum uric acid levels and disease activity in gout
key_support: Higher purine intake, especially animal sources, was associated with gout exacerbation, but findings across diet changes and serum urate were variable.
limitations: Evidence base included mainly observational designs; source type matters and further research is needed.
